memory_update.text: DSGX is the cleanest underfollowed mid-cap candidate for tariff/customs/global-trade compliance software exposure; prioritize later verification of revenue materiality and policy-driven growth.

ULS adds a TIC/certification lane to the node: policy-driven proof-of-compliance may show up in testing, certification, auditing, record keeping, and market-surveillance demand rather than in customs software alone.
Customs brokers with digital tariff-analysis tools, such as CHRW, may be second-order beneficiaries of trade-policy volatility, but exposure is diluted by broader freight-cycle economics.

Several highly relevant global-trade-management assets are private, delisted, or non-US-listed, including e2open after WiseTech acquisition and Dun & Bradstreet after Clearlake acquisition; later layers should avoid treating old tickers as currently investable US-listed candidates.

node: Tariff, customs, domestic-content, and supply-chain compliance infrastructure
summary: Expanded the direct-public-company universe for the compliance-infrastructure node. The strongest underfollowed lane is not tariff-protected manufacturing but software, data, customs-brokerage workflow, tariff-analysis tools, and testing/certification services that help importers, exporters, and regulated manufacturers prove classification, origin, admissibility, safety, and restricted-party compliance. The list intentionally mixes reference platforms with lower-mindshare direct beneficiaries; no buy/sell view is implied.
